newsitem.title: UK: IBCA assigns individual B rating to Keppel Bank.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns individual B rating to Keppel Bank.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it assigned an individual B rating to Singapore's Keppel Bank, and also assigned it a legal rating of 3.
Keppel Bank is 64 percent owned by Keppel Corporation, a large government-linked conglomerate.

IBCA said in a statement that Keppel Bank had an adequate overall financial profile. Its assets and equity had grown at a much faster rate than the Big Four Singapore banks but it was less profitable.
"The lower profitability is due to previous overprovisioning and low offshore banking income which results in a relatively high tax rate," it said.
"Keppel's expense ratios, while on the high side, are the result of a higher level of provisioning. With the provisioning removed, they are only slightly higher than those of the Big Four.

"Keppel's adequate overall financial profile is a reflection of high capitalisation and excellent asset quality, rather than profitability. Its capital adequacy ratio is much higher than the regulatory requirement and non-performing loans are low, even for a Singapore bank," the statement said.
